summary: Seventh-pass independent review of T79's repair of T76 F-001..F-004 and the orchestrator's own follow-up fix (security.ts:801, T79#F-005), on branch codex/agent-first-core at base 0bc6418. Stage 1: all four rows PASS, one with a caveat. Row 1 (enumeration axis): re-derived independently; the six mechanisms are sound and a broad non-keyword-scoped repo sweep found no seventh mechanism, but T79's execution within mechanism 5 (self-hosted checked-in copies) was keyword-bound rather than a full-content comparison against the generator each copy mirrors -- a full byte-diff surfaces a real, previously-undiscovered, pre-existing drift (F-001). Row 2 (the six corrections): all verified present and accurate against measured code, both directions checked, no new over- or under-claim introduced. Row 3 (pinning): both new regressions (security-pre-push.test.ts, templates.test.ts) run GREEN (12 pass / 0 fail / 32 expect(), matching T79's own count) and independently confirmed load-bearing by applying their own assertion predicates to the OLD text quoted verbatim in prior review artifacts (since this review is read-only on production files and cannot literally revert-and-rerun) -- every predicate flips false against the OLD text and true against current, matching the real GREEN run. The 'three unpinnable' claim is overstated: two of the three (docs/docs/modules.md, .metaproject/modules/security.md) are merely unpinned, using a pin idiom (readFile + assert, no generator seam required) this repo already uses in src/cli-reference-coverage.test.ts (F-002). Row 4 (orchestrator's security.ts:801 fix): verified right and complete (gateway now named); swept the whole file twice (28- and 37-match keyword sweeps, both undercounted by the compacted summary to 4 shown, raw read directly) and found no second site with the same defect -- every other match is an internal comment or a plain value echo. New finding F-001: this repo's own checked-in .metaproject/modules/security.md still carries the pre-T75 stale section-14 self-protection sentence ('a mode downgrade is always surfaced as a finding'), which T70/T75 already established is false in the generator function but which this on-disk self-hosted copy was never regenerated to match -- confirmed pre-existing (already stale at HEAD, untouched by this session's own WIP diff to the same file) and evading every prior sweep because the claim family falls outside the 'advisory|enforced|gateway|mode-gated|secret/critical|needs-approval' keyword list every probe from T70 through T79 used. Minor, not blocking: the actual runtime behaviour is correct, only the self-hosted static copy is stale. F-002 names the cheap pin available for both remaining 'unpinnable' sites. Per RESIDUALS.md's own recorded rule, neither finding meets the one exception (blocker, reproduced on a public boundary), so both are classified for the residual list, not a new fix round. Full dispatch-scope test suite run twice independently: bun test src/lib src/commands src/security src/health -> 2147 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail / 8517 expect() both times; typecheck clean; eslint on the 7 changed files clean (0 errors). src/security/detect/exfil.test.ts (the other worker's in-flight file) run separately and excluded from this review's verdict per dispatch instruction -- clean (58/0) at time of measurement but not attributed either way. No production, test, or documentation file was modified by this review; file hashes are identical start to end for every file read.

findings.problem: This repo's own checked-in copy of the security manifest (mechanism 5 in T79's enumeration; produced by renderSecurityManifest() and refreshed by `keryx update`) still reads 'A `configChecksum` mismatch or a mode downgrade is always surfaced as a finding plus an incident entry (self-protection, specification.md 14).' T70 F-003 established this is false and T75 corrected it -- but only in the generator function's return value. self-protect.ts has exactly one findings.push (the checksum arm); the mode-downgrade and disabled-policy arms each push a warning + an incident, never a finding, so a mode downgrade never moves the gate. This on-disk file was never regenerated for that fix: git show HEAD:.metaproject/modules/security.md already contains the stale sentence (predates this whole review chain), and this session's own WIP diff for the file touches only lines 45-51 (a separate, unrelated fix), not 88-89.
findings.impact: AC8's 'no artifact reaching a user or an agent describes behaviour the code does not have' fails on this specific site, in the false-confidence direction: a reader believes a mode-downgrade attack is caught as a finding (and therefore visible in the gate-relevant findings list) when it is actually only a warning+incident that does not move the gate or exit code. Blast radius is narrower than a shipped-into-every-project site (this file is self-hosted, this-repo-only), so severity stays minor, matching T70's original rating for the same claim. Not a working bypass: the actual runtime behaviour is correct; only this static checked-in copy is stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate .metaproject/modules/security.md from the corrected renderSecurityManifest() (run `keryx update`, or hand-align lines 88-89 to the generator's current sentence). Add the pin named in T80#F-002 -- an equality check between this file and its generator -- so a self-hosted copy drifting from a generator-only fix cannot recur silently again.

findings.problem: T79-implementation.md's pinning table calls docs/docs/modules.md and .metaproject/modules/security.md unpinnable because 'no generator seam exists.' A pin does not require a render* function -- only a way to read the shipped text and assert on it. src/cli-reference-coverage.test.ts already does exactly this, today, for cli-reference.md, index.md, mkdocs.yml, architecture.md and commands/workspace.ts (readFile + toContain/regex), none of which is generated either. The same idiom pins modules.md's Exit cells and init.ts:497's prompt string at effectively zero cost. For .metaproject/modules/security.md specifically, an even stronger pin exists: an equality check between the on-disk file and renderSecurityManifest()'s live output -- using the generator that already exists for this exact file, contradicting 'no generator seam' for this one in particular.
findings.impact: Not a code defect; a gap in this phase's own verification rigor. T80#F-001 is live proof of the cost: the exact drift this pin would catch immediately has been sitting in the tracked tree, undetected, through six review rounds specifically because no such pin exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to src/cli-reference-coverage.test.ts (or a sibling docs-drift.test.ts): (a) readFile+toContain/not.toContain for docs/docs/modules.md's scan-mcp/hooks-install Exit cells; (b) readFile+toContain for src/commands/init.ts:497's prompt string; (c) an equality (or normalized-equality) test between .metaproject/modules/security.md and renderSecurityManifest(), and between .metaproject/core/security/README.md and renderSecurityCoreReadme() -- the highest-value of the three, since it protects the whole file against any future drift, not just one sentence.
findings.evidence: src/cli-reference-coverage.test.ts read in full (228 lines): every one of its 7 tests reads a doc or source file directly via readFile and asserts on the returned string; none calls a render* function. bun src/cli.ts ctx rg "modules.md" src --glob '*.test.ts' -> 0 matches, confirming docs/docs/modules.md has no existing test coverage to extend. T80-manifest-drift.ts's own run demonstrates the equality-with-generator pin is mechanically trivial.
